subtopics.title: Signal Attenuation and Path Loss
subtopics.summary: Why wireless signal strength decreases: electromagnetic radiation attenuates as it passes through matter (e.g., walls) and disperses even in free space, so received power falls as sender-receiver distance grows.

subtopics.title: Interference and Multipath Propagation
subtopics.summary: How wireless signals are corrupted by other radio sources transmitting in the same frequency band, and how reflections off objects cause multipath propagation where multiple copies of a signal arrive at the receiver.

subtopics.title: SNR and Bit Error Rates
subtopics.summary: The relationship between signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and bit error rate (BER) on a wireless link, and how changing channel conditions and distance cause bit errors.

subtopics.title: Wireless Link Rates and Coverage Ranges
subtopics.summary: Comparison of the key characteristics of popular wireless network standards: their transmission rates and coverage distances, and how these vary with distance, channel conditions, and number of users.

subtopics.title: CDMA: Code Division Multiple Access
subtopics.summary: Introduction to CDMA as a shared-medium access protocol used in wireless networks, where senders encode their bits using unique code sequences so multiple users can transmit simultaneously over the same spectrum.
